footer.blurb: Kainku gathers Indonesian textiles — batik, tenun, songket, and jumputan — and sells them by the metre, with the width, weight, and region of origin stated plainly.

about.title: Fabric, described as it is
about.lead: We built Kainku because buying cloth online so often feels like guesswork. The photograph looks good, but the width, the weight, and the origin are rarely stated.

mission.title: What we do
mission.body: Kainku is a catalogue of Indonesian textiles sold by the metre. Every listing states the usable width in centimetres, the weight in gsm, the fibre content, and the region the motif comes from.
mission.body2: Each fabric is shown in three views: how it drapes, a macro crop of the weave, and a folded stack. The point is simple — you should be able to judge both the scale of the motif and the texture before you order, not after the parcel arrives.

values.title: Four things we hold to
values.lead: No grand promises — just working habits you can check for yourself on any product page.

origin.title: Origin, stated
origin.text: Every fabric names the city and province its motif comes from. Where we do not know the origin, we do not invent one.

measure.title: Measurements, given
measure.text: Width in centimetres, weight in gsm, and the cutting increment in metres. All of it is written down before you add anything to the cart.

transparency.title: Priced by the metre
transparency.text: Prices are always shown per metre, with no charges appearing at the last step. Shipping only appears once you have chosen a service.

care.title: Care instructions
care.text: Each fabric carries washing and storage notes matched to its fibre content and the way it was dyed.

items.title: Assembling the catalogue
items.text: Compiling motifs from across the archipelago together with their technical characteristics: width, weight, and fibre content.

items.title: Building the viewing system
items.text: Creating three standard views for every fabric so buyers can compare motif scale fairly from one product to the next.

items.title: Preparing the ordering flow
items.text: Designing a cart and checkout that work in metres, including per-product cutting increments and minimum order lengths.

items.title: Payment and inventory integration
items.text: Connecting a real payment gateway, stock management, and couriers. This work is tracked in TODO.md in the repository.

honesty.title: How far along is this site?
honesty.body: This is a demonstration build. The catalogue, cart, and checkout flows work fully on the interface side, but they are not yet connected to a payment gateway, an inventory system, or a courier. No payment is processed and no order is actually dispatched.

faq.title: Questions we get most often
faq.lead: The things people usually want settled before ordering cloth by the metre.
faq.stillStuckText: Send us your question and we will reply during working hours.

items.q: Is the fabric sold by the metre or by the piece?
items.a: By the metre. Each product states its minimum order and its cutting increment on the product page — most can be cut in half-metre steps.

items.q: How do I work out how many metres I need?
items.a: The Size Guide lists estimates for several garment types on a 115 cm width. Treat those as starting points; directional motifs usually need extra.

items.q: What does gsm mean in the product details?
items.a: Gsm is grams per square metre, a measure of fabric weight. The higher the number, the heavier and thicker the cloth. Fabrics between 120 and 140 gsm tend to be light and fluid, while 200 gsm and above feels noticeably more structured.

items.q: Will the colour on screen match the real fabric?
items.a: Not exactly. Every screen renders colour differently, and dye lots vary between production runs. We include a macro view of the weave to help, and swatches can be requested through the contact page.

items.q: Will the fabric shrink after washing?
items.a: Natural fibres such as cotton generally shrink on the first wash. We recommend washing the cloth before cutting if you are sewing a garment.
The checkout page offers bank transfer, virtual account, e-wallet, and cash on delivery. In this demonstration build none of them is connected to a payment gateway, so no money is taken.
Transit estimates for each service are shown at checkout. Those figures are working-day estimates and exclude the time needed to prepare the order.

items.q: Can I return fabric that has already been cut?
items.a: Cut-to-order fabric cannot normally be returned, unless there is a material defect or the wrong item was sent. The details are on the Returns & Exchanges page.

sizeGuide.title: How many metres do you need?
sizeGuide.lead: Fabric estimates for common sewing projects, calculated on a 115 cm width.

disclaimer.title: These are estimates, not guarantees.
disclaimer.body: Actual requirements depend on body measurements, the pattern you use, the fabric width, and the direction of the motif. For directional or large-scale motifs, add 15–25% to be safe.

rows.note: Depends on length and sleeve style.

howToMeasure.title: Working out your requirement
howToMeasure.body: Measure the longest piece on your pattern, multiply it by the number of pieces that will not fit side by side across the fabric width, then add 10% for seam allowances and adjustments. If the motif has to line up across a seam, add one full pattern repeat for each join.

shrinkage.title: Shrinkage
shrinkage.body: Cotton and other natural fibres typically shrink 3–5% on the first wash. Wash and dry the cloth before cutting so the finished garment does not change size later.
